 Cheryl McCloud, USA TODAY NETWORK - Florida Updated Tue, October 20, 2026 at 1:19 PM UTC Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. The day when we turn our clocks back is less than two weeks away.
 Daylight saving time will end at 2 a.m. local time on Nov. 1 as we "fall back" and move our clocks back one hour to return to standard time.

 Many Americans want to end the twice-annual clock changes, but  polls differ  on whether standard time or daylight saving time should be permanent.

 "People are sick and tired of having to change their clocks twice a year. It is foolish, inconvenient and, in some cases, very costly," President Trump posted on TruthSocial Aug. 12.
 The Sunshine Protection Act was voted on by the House of Representatives July 14, allowing states to make daylight saving time permanent, although states can opt out.
 ➤  Here's which states favor daylight saving time and where Florida stands 
 H.R. 139, known as the Sunshine Protection Act , was filed Jan. 3, 2025, by Rep. Vern Buchanan , Florida-District 16. Buchanan has brought the Sunshine Protection Act before each Congress since 2018. 
 Advertisement Advertisement The Senate version of the bill,  S. 29 , has been in limbo since it was referred to the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation on Jan. 7, 2025, where it still was as of Oct. 20.
 Here are quick answers to 10 of the most common questions Florida residents have been asking about the upcoming time change.
 When do clocks fall back in Florida in 2026?
 Daylight saving time for 2026 ends on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 2 a.m. local time, when clocks will "fall back" an hour to 1 a.m.
 The change means a return to standard time, which brings earlier sunrises and earlier sunsets.
 When will Florida spring forward again for daylight saving time?
 Daylight saving time begins on the second Sunday in March each year.
 Advertisement Advertisement ➤ Daylight saving time to end in Florida. List of fall back dates till 2036 
 In 2027, Floridians will move clocks ahead one hour at 2 a.m. local time on March 14, losing an hour of sleep but gaining more daylight in the evenings.
 Is Florida ending daylight saving time?
 No. Florida currently observes daylight saving time and makes twice-yearly clock changes.
 While state lawmakers — and voters — have expressed support for permanent daylight saving time since 2018, that change has not been approved by Congress.
 Will Florida ever stay on daylight saving time year-round?
 For Florida or any other state to stop changing the clock and stay on daylight saving time year-round, Congress must approve making daylight saving time permanent and the president needs to sign it into law.
 Advertisement Advertisement Under the Sunshine Protection Act, Florida has said the state intends to adopt year-round daylight saving time if or when federal law allows it.
 Do you gain or lose an hour when Florida falls back?
 You lose an hour when clocks move forward in March and gain an extra hour of sleep when clocks move back in November.

The Mayor of London's New Year's Eve Fireworks show is launched from the London Eye, with Queen Elizabeth Tower (commonly known as Big Ben) in the foreground, to mark the new year on January 1, 2026 in London, England. (Leon Neal, Getty Images) Why does Florida still change the clocks every year?
 In 2018, Florida became the  first state to enact legislation  to stay on daylight saving time all year round.
 The Florida  Legislature approved HB 1013 , the Sunshine Protection Act, with a vote of 103 to 11 in the House and 33 to 2 in the Florida Senate. Sen. Rick Scott, who was the Florida governor at the time,  signed it .
 Advertisement Advertisement And there it stopped, because making daylight saving time requires the repeal of the federal mandate. So without congressional approval, nothing could change.
 Until Congress changes federal law, Florida must continue changing clocks twice a year.
 How will the time change affect sunrises and sunsets in Florida?
 The number of hours of daylight remains the same no matter whether we're under daylight saving time or standard time.
 What changes is when those hours occur.
 ➤ Standard time vs DST. See Florida sunrise, sunsets times for each 
 After clocks fall back in November, the sun rises earlier and sets earlier, based on the clock.
 After clocks spring forward in March, sunrises occur later and sunsets occur later, providing more daylight in the evening.
 What is the latest on the Sunshine Protection Act?
 The U.S. House voted 308-117 July 14 to make daylight saving time permanent, sending H.R. 139 to the Senate for consideration.
 Advertisement Advertisement The measure has not been approved by the U.S. Senate approval and then sent to the president for his signature, which is needed before it could become law.
 ➤ Read the bills in their entirety:  S. 29  and   H.R. 139 
 The Senate is on recess until Nov. 9, after daylight saving time ends.
 The Sunshine Protection Act does allow states to opt out of permanent daylight saving time in favor of permanent standard time if legislation is passed through their respective state legislatures, Buchanan said. States can do so right up until the bill is enacted.
 Which states do not observe daylight saving time?
 Hawaii and most of Arizona — except the Navajo Reservation — do not observe daylight saving time. They remain on standard time all year.
 Advertisement Advertisement Five U.S. territories do not observe daylight saving time:
  U.S. Virgin Islands 
 American Samoa
 Guam
 Northern Mariana Islands
 Puerto Rico 
 Would Florida permanently stay on daylight saving time or standard time?
 Florida's Sunshine Protection Act calls for the state to stay on daylight saving time year-round, not standard time, if Congress passes and the president signs it into law.
 Bonus question: Could Florida stay on standard time?
 Yes. Under current federal law, states may choose to stay on standard time year-round.
 That option does not require federal approval, but Florida has not pursued that option.
 Is it daylight saving time or Daylight Savings Time?
 It's daylight saving time, no s and no capital letters.
